facts.text: The README's quick-start example makes block-cpu-single-task1-v0 and steps it with an action sampled from its action space
block-cpu-single-task1-v0 is registered with entry point ocbench.envs.block_env:BlockEnv, max_episode_steps=1250 and kwargs env_type='single', task_id=1
ocbench.make returns gymnasium.make(env_name, **kwargs) for CPU environments
BlockEnv subclasses ManipulationEnv and the single env_type installs one cube
The single task is named move and its goal position is [0.425, 0.0, 0.03]
The action space is a Box of seven float32 values from -1 to 1
The per-joint action deltas are 0.18, 0.18, 0.18, 0.36, 0.36, 0.36 and 0.12 times action_delta_scale
unnormalize_action clips every action value to [-1, 1] and multiplies it by the joint action deltas
ManipulationEnv defaults physics_timestep to 0.002 s and control_timestep to 0.02 s
set_timesteps sets the number of physics steps per control step to control_timestep divided by physics_timestep
CustomMuJoCoEnv.step applies the action, steps the model nstep times, computes the flags, observation and reward, and returns the five-tuple
The state observation concatenates joint positions, joint velocities, the scaled effector position, cos and sin of the effector yaw, the scaled gripper opening and gripper contact
BlockEnv appends every cube's three positions, four quaternion values, cos yaw and sin yaw to the observation
The observation space is a Box from -inf to +inf with the observation shape
The reward is 1.0 when success is true, failure is false and the state is healthy; otherwise 0.0
A cube is successful when its distance to the target mocap is at most 0.04
The episode terminates when terminate_at_success and success, or failure, or the state is not healthy
terminate_at_success defaults to True
CustomMuJoCoEnv.truncate_episode returns False, so the environment itself never truncates
A reset calls Gymnasium's reset(seed=seed, options=options), initializes the episode and returns the observation and info

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds Gymnasium's generator and the MuJoCo model then advances deterministically, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a trajectory; this package's fake draws its start state from Python's random.Random, so the same seed gives a different trajectory on the fake and upstream

gaps: the upstream model is MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics with contacts (F1): the UR5e and Robotiq contacts, actuator forces, inverse kinematics and the block task are not modelled by the fake, which advances a simple analytic state instead
the fake does not compute task success, the target tolerance, the reward or termination; it returns reward 0.0, terminated False and truncates at the registered step limit
the fake draws its start state from Python's random.Random, upstream uses Gymnasium's seeded numpy generator, so a seed gives different state vectors on the two
the fake returns a flat list of Python floats; upstream returns a numpy concatenation
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
